name: 992.1 Generation
description:
Unveiled at the Los Angeles Auto Show on 28 November 2018, the 992 arrived as the eighth generation of the 911 and as the moment the wide body stopped being a privilege of the Turbo models: for the first time every car in the range — Carrera, Targa, GTS, GT3 — carries the flared rear arches and 20-inch front/21-inch rear wheels that had previously marked out only the top performers. Styled under Michael Mauer by Ben Baum, it grew 45 mm (1.8 in) wider than the 991 on an unchanged 2,450 mm (96.5 in) wheelbase, added aluminium body panels, pop-out door handles and a full-length rear light bar, and put the driver's instruments back into two screens either side of a central analogue rev counter.

The first phase, known as 992.1, ran entirely on turbocharged flat-sixes. The 2,981 cc unit made 385 PS in the Carrera and Carrera T, 450 PS in the S models and 480 PS in the GTS, while a 3,745 cc twin-VTG engine covered the 550 PS Sport Classic, the 580 PS Turbo and the 650 PS Turbo S. An entirely new eight-speed PDK was the only gearbox at launch; the seven-speed manual reached the S and 4S in 2019, and the six-speed GT manual arrived with the GT3 in 2021. Porsche Wet Mode — acoustic sensors in the wheel arches reading the surface and adjusting stability control, wing position and gearbox response — and the 10.9-inch Porsche Communication Management display were both new for the generation.

The naturally aspirated half of the range returned with the 510 PS GT3 in February 2021, launched simultaneously in swan-neck-wing and Touring form, and fed the 525 PS GT3 RS of August 2022: 860 kg of downforce at 285 km/h, a DRS-style rear wing and a Nürburgring time Porsche later certified at 6:44.848. The collector half was just as prolific. The 992-unit Targa 4S Heritage Design Edition opened Porsche's Heritage Design strategy in 2020; the 1,250-car Sport Classic put a detuned 3.7-litre engine, a manual gearbox and rear-wheel drive under the Turbo body in 2022; and 2023 brought both the 1,380 kg manual 911 S/T and the 2,500-unit 911 Dakar, which can raise its ride height until it has 191 mm (7.5 in) of ground clearance.

The 992.1 phase closed with the 1,974-unit 911 Turbo 50 Years — a number taken from the year the first Turbo was shown — and the 911 S/T, the lightest 911 of the generation at 1,380 kg (3,042 lb) in DIN trim. In May 2024 Porsche launched the 992.2 phase with the T-Hybrid Carrera GTS, bringing electric assistance to the 911 for the first time and ending six years of pure-combustion 992.1s.

variants.description: Joined the range in July 2019 as the entry point to the eighth generation, nine months after the Carrera S and 4S debuted in Los Angeles. It uses the same 2,981 cc twin-turbo flat-six as the S car but with model-specific turbochargers — smaller turbine and compressor wheels — to make 283 kW (385 PS; 379 hp) and 450 Nm (332 lb-ft) from 1,950 rpm. Only an eight-speed PDK was offered: the manual gearbox was reserved for the S, the 4S and later the Carrera T. variants.description: The car that launched the 992. Porsche chose the Los Angeles Auto Show on 28 November 2018 to unveil the Carrera S and Carrera 4S, and the 3.0-litre biturbo was the headline: 331 kW (450 PS; 443 hp) at 6,500 rpm and 530 Nm (391 lb-ft) between 2,300 and 5,000 rpm, both new highs for a Carrera. A brand-new eight-speed PDK was standard, with a seven-speed manual added for 2020 model years — fitted with Sport Chrono as standard. The S sprints to 100 km/h in 3.7 seconds, or 3.5 with Sport Chrono, and runs to 308 km/h. Coupé and Cabriolet, and the basis for the Sport Classic and the whole 992.1 GT family.

variants.description: Arrived in September 2019, four months after the rear-drive Carrera, bringing Porsche Traction Management and the wide body to the entry-level 911. The engine is the Carrera's 2,981 cc twin-turbo — 283 kW (385 PS; 379 hp) at 6,500 rpm with 450 Nm (332 lb-ft) from 1,950 rpm — but the front axle drive was redeveloped for the extra mass, and the car carries roughly 50 kg more than the rear-drive Coupé. variants.description: Seven months after the Turbo S, in July 2020, the 992.1 Turbo arrived as the cheapest route to 580 PS. The 3,745 cc twin-turbo flat-six uses symmetrical VTG turbochargers with a slightly smaller compressor wheel than the S, giving 427 kW (580 PS; 572 hp) at 6,750 rpm and 750 Nm (553 lb-ft) between 2,500 and 5,000 rpm — with no overboost time limit. The result matches the outgoing 997-generation Turbo S: under three seconds to 100 km/h, in fact 2.8, and 320 km/h (199 mph). The Turbo keeps the S's side intakes and rear wing logic but gives up the twin oval sport exhaust for four round tips, cast-iron discs with red calipers and five-lug wheels; almost everything else was optional on the S.

variants.description: Presented on 3 March 2020, the 992.1 Turbo S was the most powerful 911 Porsche had built. A brand-new 3,745 cm³ boxer with two VTG turbochargers — based on the Carrera engine but with a shorter stroke — makes 478 kW (650 PS; 641 hp) at 6,750 rpm and 800 Nm (590 lb-ft) from 2,500 rpm. The air intake moved from the rear wings to directly behind the engine, and the wings now house the air filters. Standard equipment ran to PDCC, rear-axle steering, adaptive anti-roll bars and ceramic composite brakes, while the two-stage rear wing generated 15 per cent more downforce than the outgoing car. It covered 100 km/h in 2.7 seconds and 330 km/h, and Sport Auto timed it at 7:17.3 on the Nordschleife.

The 3,996 cc naturally aspirated flat-six makes 386 kW (525 PS; 518 hp) and 465 Nm, and for the first time is mated to a six-speed manual — with a clutch and single-mass flywheel developed for the car that together save 10.5 kg, plus rigid rocker arms in place of hydraulic valve adjustment. CFRP front wings and bonnet, GT3 RS doors weighing just 9.5 kg, and a double-bubble roof. At 1,380 kg (3,042 lb) DIN it is the lightest 911 of the generation: 0–100 km/h in 3.7 seconds, 300 km/h limited.

variants.description: The second of Porsche's four Heritage Design collector's cars, revealed on 28 April 2022. It takes the wide Turbo body and removes everything that made the Turbo difficult to love: all-wheel drive, the deployable spoiler, PDK and the 580 PS tune. What is left is a rear-wheel-drive 992 with a seven-speed manual, a fixed ducktail rear spoiler and ducts in its own spoiler skin instead of fender intakes, a CFRP bonnet, and a 3,745 cm³ twin-turbo detuned to 405 kW (550 PS; 542 hp) and 600 Nm (443 lb-ft) because the manual could not take the Turbo's 750 Nm. Spring rates at the front were softened for the missing driven axle. At 1,250 units it remains the most powerful manual 911 in production.

It is PDK only, and around 100 kg heavier than the Carrera 4 at 1,665 kg (3,671 lb) because of the retractable roof structure, with 330 mm brake discs front and rear against the 4S's 350 mm. Porsche Traction Management splits torque to all four wheels, PTV Plus is optional, and the roof panel stows electrically under the rear deck.

variants.description: All-wheel drive plus the GTS's 480 PS made this the quickest 992.1 Carrera in production. The 353 kW (480 PS; 473 hp) and 570 Nm (420 lb-ft) 2,981 cm³ twin-turbo drives all four wheels through Porsche Traction Management, with GTS-tuned PASM dampers, rear helper springs and the Turbo's brake hardware. Coupé and Cabriolet were both offered with the eight-speed PDK or a seven-speed manual. The Coupé reaches 100 km/h in 3.3 seconds with Sport Chrono and 308 km/h (191 mph); the Cabriolet manages 3.5 seconds. An optional Aerokit swapped the retractable spoiler for a fixed rear wing, and a Lightweight Design package from November 2021 cut up to 25 kg.

variants.description: The third of the five 992.1 GTS models, and the only one that keeps the Targa's extra mass over the equivalent coupé. It uses the same 353 kW (480 PS; 473 hp) and 570 Nm (420 lb-ft) twin-turbo as the Carrera GTS, all-wheel drive, and either the eight-speed PDK or a seven-speed manual with a shortened lever. Unusually for a GTS, Porsche gave it the Targa 4S chassis — including PASM, rear-axle steering and the roof's structural weight — which costs both performance and refinement: 0–100 km/h in 3.5 seconds with Sport Chrono and 308 km/h (191 mph), from 1,685 kg (3,715 lb) DIN. Launched in June 2021 alongside the other GTS models, and the basis of the 750-unit 911 Edition 50 Years Porsche Design.

variants.description: Marking fifty years of the 911 Turbo, this 992.1 special edition was unveiled at Monterey in August 2024 and limited to 1,974 units — the year the first Turbo was shown. Mechanically it is a Turbo S: 3,745 cm³ twin-turbo flat-six, 478 kW (650 PS; 641 hp) and 800 Nm (590 lb-ft), all-wheel drive and the eight-speed PDK, with the chassis lowered 10 mm and a sport exhaust. The styling does the celebrating: a new Turbonite metallic on the fuel cap, crest, decklid inlays and Exclusive Design wheels; Anthracite Grey on the wing and intake trim; a rear badge showing a turbocharger and '1974–2024'; side graphics from the 1973 911 RSR Turbo; and MacKenzie tartan on the seat centres and door cards.
